Task:
Implement Memoizer.wrap(&computation), returning a callable that invokes computation at most once no matter how many times the callable itself is called - including when computation returns a falsy value like nil or false - and forwards whatever arguments each call is given through to computation on the one invocation that actually runs it.

content.text:
```ruby
module Memoizer
  def self.wrap(&computation)
    called = false
    result = nil

    lambda do |*args, &block|
      unless called
        result = computation.call(*args, &block)
        called = true
      end
      result
    end
  end
end
```

This returns a lambda that, on its first invocation (with whatever arguments/block it receives), calls `computation` exactly once, stores the result (even if it's `nil` or `false`), and marks itself as having run via the separate `called` flag — so falsy results are still correctly remembered and not recomputed. Every subsequent call, regardless of the arguments passed, simply returns the memoized result without invoking `computation` again.
